newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Kabila invited to OAU summit as Congo leader.
newsitem.headline: Kabila invited to OAU summit as Congo leader.

text.p: Laurent Kabila, self-declared president of the new Democratic Republic of Congo, will attend an Organisation of African Unity summit in Zimbabwe in June as a head of state, the OAU announced on Thursday.

OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim, speaking ahead of the June 2-4 summit of African leaders in Harare, said he wanted Kabila to launch a "new and broad-based political dispensation based on accommodation, unity and cohesion" in the former Zaire.

Salim appealed to African countries and the international community to provide support, understanding and cooperation to Kabila's administration. The OAU was showing the way with Kabila in Harare as a "fully fledged African leader".
Salim urged Africans to learn from Zaire's experience, allowing their people a choice and decision on governance.
"The events which took place in the Democratic Republic of Congo provide a clear example of what can happen when people are denied the democratic option," Salim said in a statement.
Th statement marked the 34th anniversary of the OAU on May 25.

"The Zaire experience needs to be reflected upon (by) our continent as we forge ahead to consolidate peace and stability...through empowering our people in deciding how they are governed, by whom and for what period," Salim added.
Salim thanked West African countries for their efforts in ending the seven-year civil war in Liberia.
"Due to their efforts Liberia is to have democratic elections on July 19 where the ballot and not the bullet will decide the destiny of its people," Salim said.
He said there were encouraging signs that conflicts in Sierra Leone, Burundi and Somalia would end peacefully.
He appealed to member states to take seriously the task of building an African Economic Community "which constitutes a unique framework for collective recovery and development".
Salim also said he had decided to seek a third term as OAU secretary-general "because I know I enjoy the support from many African leaders across the divide."
